clue.text: Caught over far from sensible contract

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
on means over, as in resting on top of
someone far from sensible is dense, slow-witted

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's verdict on a foolish batting deal: out caught over an unwise contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for an agreement, but it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense something is to make it smaller or more compact, a synonym of the verb contract.

clue.text: This French mount is red

parts.note: ce is French for this
to mount is to rise

explanation.surface: A French mountain glows red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a cherry-coloured shade of red.

clue.text: Not in a strange country

indicators.note: strange suggests something altered, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feels out of place abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people or state, a country.

clue.text: Blunders a defaulter committed in time

indicators.note: committed in suggests being put inside, as into an institution

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is one who deserts or fails his side

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by a debtor who failed to pay up on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committed in' signals insertion, as a person is committed into an institution; a rat is a deserter, one who defaults on loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed mistakes, especially printing errors.

clue.text: Standing still with men only 2

parts.note: a stag party is for men only
the answer to the clue 2-down

explanation.surface: A men-only gathering goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2' points to the solution of 2-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of inactivity, with no flow or growth.

clue.text: A youngster holding woman to be a heavenly being

indicators.note: one piece holding another means it is placed around it

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
her stands for a woman, the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A child carrying a woman is likened to an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals one piece wrapped around another; 'A youngster' is a single piece, not A plus a word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition a cherub is an angel of a lower order, often painted as a winged child.

clue.text: A dependant not paid to swallow annoyance

indicators.note: one word swallows another by taking it inside

parts.note: HON abbreviates honorary, an unpaid post
anger is strong annoyance

explanation.surface: An unpaid hanger-about has to put up with irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' signals insertion; 'not paid' is the abbreviation for honorary, as in an honorary secretary who works unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a parasite who attaches himself to another for benefit.

clue.text: Prompting soldiers to guard the monarch

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to mind something is to guard it
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Troops are urged to protect the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a prompt that jogs the memory.

clue.text: Scoring highest is sweet

definitions.meaning: hitting the centre of a dartboard

explanation.surface: A darts player wins a candy.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a target gives the top score in darts; it is also a round boiled mint candy.

clue.text: An honoured member of society or a rat in disposition?

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the preceding words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Is this distinguished clubman really a rat at heart?
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, but signals an arrangement of OR A RAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Rotary, an international service club, is invited to join as a respected local figure.

clue.text: Top-coat for which a quarter specify a figure

parts.note: east is one quarter of the compass, abbreviated E
to name something is to specify it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A decorator chooses the final coat by naming a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy paint used as the final finishing layer on woodwork.

clue.text: Carol gets drink in, being a good sort

indicators.note: the drink is put in the middle of the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A carol singer who brings drinks for everyone is a decent person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting person is generous and fair-minded, playing the game in spirit.

clue.text: He did wrong retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to have sinned is to have done wrong

explanation.surface: A man misbehaved and then withdrew from public life.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis is a man's first name, and the pronoun stands for any male person.

clue.text: Airily written English article indeed!

parts.note: the is the definite article
really is used like indeed for emphasis

explanation.surface: A lightly written piece of English prose provokes surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means light and delicate as air, so the adverb means in an airy way.

clue.text: Place beside Oriental railway providing material for a writer

parts.note: a station is a place or post where someone is put
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A shop next to an eastern railway sells writing supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery means paper, envelopes and pens, the supplies used for writing.

clue.text: Silly ass tried for causing appalling accident

indicators.note: silly suggests letters behaving foolishly, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A foolish donkey trial caused a terrible mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a catastrophic event.

clue.text: Taking a break from work quietly when in some discomfort

indicators.note: when in means the work and quiet letters go inside the discomfort word

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
OP is short for opus, a musical work
p is piano, softly in music

explanation.surface: Downing tools quietly because of some pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when in' signals insertion; 'work' is the musical opus abbreviation and 'quietly' the musical piano sign, both going inside together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping means halting or pausing, ceasing activity for a while.

clue.text: Wagtail-treat it possibly as a different bird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter
possibly signals the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Feeding a wagtail might attract another species instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wagtail' must be split: the tail of WAG gives G, and 'possibly' shuffles TREAT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common European songbird of the titmouse family, distinct from the wagtail.

clue.text: Put in extra large E in printed form

indicators.note: the outsize and E letters go in the middle of the rearranged word
to form is to shape, so the letters of the word printed are reshaped

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A typesetter inserts a big capital E into a printed page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges the word printed into INTERPD, and 'in' places the outsize letters and E inside that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to place something between other things, to insert it.

clue.text: Vehicle retained by corrupt firm

indicators.note: retained by means held inside the other word

parts.note: rot is corruption or decay
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A bus kept by a dishonest company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retained by' signals insertion. 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective meaning sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means strong and sturdy, firmly built.

clue.text: A crossing-place for game

definitions.meaning: a structure carrying a road over a river
a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Somewhere to cross for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A span over water lets you cross; the same word names a partnership card game.

clue.text: There'll be insufficient if many land

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
earth is land or ground

explanation.surface: If lots of people arrive there will not be enough to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage of supply means not enough, a lack.

clue.text: Pop back with ring and charm

indicators.note: back means the word for pop is read in reverse

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, as is pop
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Dad returns with a ring and a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is attractiveness, the power to draw people in, like charm.

clue.text: A means of support, secure or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Whether it is secure or not, you need some backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource is a stock or supply that can be drawn on for help.

clue.text: At man suspects himself a fool." Young (Night Thoughts)

definitions.text: At man suspects himself a fool." Young (Night Thoughts)

parts.words: At man suspects himself a fool." Young (Night Thoughts)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap after its first word: Edward Young's line names the age at which a man first suspects his own folly

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Young's poem Night Thoughts says: 'At thirty man suspects himself a fool'. The missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The age named in Edward Young's poem is the number of years in three decades.

clue.text: The person starting without money has to struggle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a founder is the person who starts an enterprise
L stands for pound, the British unit of money

explanation.surface: A business founder short of cash finds things hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so FOUNDER goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to flail about clumsily, making little progress.

clue.text: Settles just claims

definitions.meaning: the verb: puts in order, corrects
fair entitlements, as in human entitlements

explanation.surface: Someone resolves fair demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrects is one sense of the verb; lawful entitlements are the plural noun.

clue.text: Enabling people to watch their food-intake?

definitions.text: Enabling people to watch their food-intake?

parts.words: Enabling people to watch their food-intake?
parts.note: read literally: teeth that come with vision, so you could keep an eye on what you bite

explanation.definitionFit: Eye teeth are the canine teeth, so called because they sit beneath the eyes.
